title: Rust in the Linux Kernel: What It Means in 2026 | Rustify
snippet:
> TL;DR: Rust was accepted into the Linux kernel in October 2022 (kernel 6.1). By 2026, Rust kernel code is shipping in production: Android's Binder IPC driver has a Rust implementation, Apple's GPU driver (asahi-gpu) is Rust, and multiple filesystem and network subsystems have Rust contributions. This is the biggest architectural change in the Linux kernel in decades.

## A New Layer: The Rust-for-Linux Framework

The groundwork for Rust modules in Linux was laid with kernel 6.1, and by version 6.8, the first experimental Rust drivers, covering areas like network PHYs and panic QR logging, were accepted. title: The (successful) end of the kernel Rust experiment [LWN.net]
snippet:
The topic of the Rust experiment was just discussed at the annual Maintainers Summit. The consensus among the assembled developers is that Rust in the kernel is no longer experimental — it is now a core part of the kernel and is here to stay. So the "experimental" tag will be coming off. Congratulations are in order for all of the Rust for Linux team.

(Stay tuned for details in our Maintainers Summit coverage.)
